title: Storyville after its official closing
summary: Hug recalls walking Basin Street as a boy when Storyville was officially closed but still active.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Did you ever get up to the Storyville area? And supposedly the pianos were playing in the Storyville area.
Well, I could say this, that I can remember walking around in that area, but of course you must remember that it closed 1918. That's correct. According to what we know or what we read about.
Well, that's what they read, but that's not what Luke's hero says, and he used to sell ice cream there.
It was still going. So he ought to know. It was still going on that, wasn't it?

Why, sure. That's what I told somebody the other night. I said, you know, I said, you know, officially it may have closed down. I said, but don't kid yourself that there wasn't a lot of it still in existence. Even when I was about maybe, say, 12 or 13 years old, when I used to go around walking around on Basin Street, I can remember Eddie Miller and I and Shockey and Julian Lane, or I could have mentioned many musicians that we used to go around there, and we used to encounter lots of the girls, you know, like they're doing today, the same thing. They were in their little cubby holes, you know, and they were operating, I'm sure. And there was still the sounds of a little piano playing here and there, you know, so I'm sure that it was still going on, even though officially it had closed down.
Well, most people don't realize that a lot of it was there. You know, where charity is now.
Right. Yeah, there were a lot of girls in there. Right. Now, Foujira, never mind, I won't put that on there. Well, Foujira says it's a lot cheaper there. Or the other world said that.
It was a lot cheaper there.
